This test consumes 1 mL of the solution to perform a flame-color test. It returns the observed color of the flame (if any).

- It uses 1 mL of the solution to perform a flame test.
- If no species are present that give a characteristic flame color, the resulting observations is "No characteristic color".

- If multiple different colors are observed, the resulting observation will be "A multi-colored flame".

3.  If a multi-colored flame is observed, you can try to remove some of the cations by precipitation and run the test again. But they have separate fourth group also "insoluble sulfide". So second group is acid-insoluble sulfide (i.e., sulfides that do not dissolve in dilute HCl). Fourth group is insoluble sulfide (maybe acid-soluble sulfides). So second group includes cations that form sulfides insoluble in dilute acid: e.g., Cu2+, Pb2+, Bi3+, Sb3+, As3+, etc. However Pb2+ already in group I? In many schemes, Pb2+ forms insoluble chloride (white precipitate) but also forms sulfide insoluble in acid. But they may have placed Pb2+ in group I (insoluble chloride). Since they already identified Ag+ only, maybe Pb2+ not present.

Thus we need to test sample for second group cations. Use sulfide reagent (H2S) in acidic medium? Usually we add H2S gas in presence of dilute HCl; cations of group II precipitate as black sulfides that are insoluble in dilute acid. So we can add H2S reagent (maybe "H2S solution" reagent).
